alternatives.why_less_likely: the few slow orders requests occurred early and were isolated; the sustained timeout burst correlates with queue buildup, not with a gradual slowdown of order processing
unanswered calls from gateway to orders only appear after the symptom onset (+69s), so they are a consequence of the overload, not the initiating cause

causal_chain.claim: orders requests experienced queuing delay (queue time up to 347ms)
gateway timed out waiting for orders after 2500ms

root_cause.summary: orders lost serving capacity after its worker limit dropped to one, causing requests to queue and eventually timeout at the gateway

verification.reason: disabling the matching condition(s) makes the incident disappear

alternatives.why_less_likely: Inventory and payments services show normal latency and error rates throughout the incident, indicating they did not slow down orders.
Although orders logged retries, they were infrequent and not sufficient to cause the observed queue buildup; the dominant factor was the worker limit reduction.

causal_chain.claim: CPU throttling of the orders service reduced its worker limit to 1.
The reduced worker count caused orders' request queue to grow and latency to rise.
Orders latency exceeded the gateway's 2500ms timeout, triggering upstream timeout errors in the gateway.
Gateway upstream timeout errors appeared as increased 5xx errors and latency, visible to users.

root_cause.summary: Orders service CPU throttled, reducing workers to 1 and causing request queue buildup and latency.
